subject: Life Skills
title: Stain Removal Principles
description: A fast breakdown of Stain Removal Principles for builders.

hook.text: Rubbing a fresh stain is the most common reaction and also the fastest way to make it permanent.

buildup.text: Rubbing pushes pigment deeper into fibers. Blotting lifts it away from the surface gently.

discovery.text: Protein stains like blood need cold water. Hot water cooks the protein and bonds it to fabric.

twist.text: Grease stains need the opposite: dish soap breaks oil bonds that cold water alone cannot touch.

climax.text: Identify the stain type first: protein, oil, or tannin. Each category demands a different approach.

punchline.text: Know the stain before you fight it.

quiz.question: Why should blood stains be treated with cold water?
options: Hot water cooks the protein and sets the stain
Blood only comes out at low temperatures
